No. 01 Out now

All Time High

“How far would you go in a mania? Every choice has a ledger. Every gain has a price.”

A moral-descent thriller told through your phone, your feeds, and a trading terminal. Chase a California fortune one “just one more trade” at a time — through a crypto mania where every gain costs something. Your choices write the ledger. Six endings.

No. 02 Coming Oct 28, 2026

1453: Fall of Constantinople

“Everyone knows the city will fall. No one knows who they’ll be that day.”

Venice, 1500. Anna Notaras is writing down testimonies of the siege, and four witnesses sit at her table — a janissary, a baker’s daughter, an engineer, a noble. They live the same fifty-three days from both sides of the walls, and their accounts don’t always agree. Your choices cross between their stories.

No. 03 Coming Nov 11, 2026

Dear Nobody

“A war you never see. A love that exists only on paper. A pen that has started to answer back.”

You are the censor reading letters between two lovers who have never met — striking words from a wartime correspondence that begins, impossibly, to answer your own pen. Every word you cut is cut from the relationship too. Six endings.

No. 04 Coming Nov 18, 2026

Please Confirm the Deceased

“The paperwork says one thing. The body says another. Sign anyway.”

You work nights at a morgue intake desk. Bodies arrive with paperwork, and the paperwork is your job — check it, question it, stamp it, send it on. Most nights the two agree. The nights they don’t are the ones you will remember. Seven nights, forty-five intakes, and instruments that tell you things the forms do not.

No. 05 Coming 30 November 2026

The Previous Owner

“Shelve carefully, and do not read the margins.”

Run a secondhand bookshop in London, 1994. Every book remembers who owned it before — pressed flowers, letters, notes in the margins. Across books that should never have met, the same hand keeps writing. You inherited the rules with the shop.

WindowsmacOS11 languagesLondon, 1994Single-player

No. 06 Coming February 2027

Per My Last Email

“Every reply is two decisions, and the second one is the real one.”

You are the newest hire on floor four at Bellwether & Locke, and the account you inherited is not a new account — it belonged to E. Vale, who is no longer with the company. Ten business days of email. You choose what you say, then you choose who sees it: reply, reply-all, forward, CC, BCC. The routing is permanent and it goes in your file. A CC that seemed polite on Day 2 is evidence on Day 9.

WindowsmacOS11 languagesTen business daysSix endings
Wishlist on Steam Play the free demo on Steam
No. 07 Coming April 2027

Town Hall

“Whatever you stamp becomes true.”

Most of the town has left, but the town hall still opens at nine. You are the clerk — the mayor is unreachable, the council hasn't met in two years, and the seal on your desk still works, which makes you the government. Permits, licenses, certificates of birth and death: the paper is a claim, your stamp is the fact. Then step out to the town map and visit what you signed — the reopened bar, the condemned house, the pier that is suddenly private property.

WindowsmacOSFirst-person 3D11 languagesSingle-player
Wishlist on Steam Play the free demo on Steam
No. 08 Coming Q2 2027

The Off-Season

“The hotel is closed for the winter. You have the keys.”

You are the winter caretaker of a seaside hotel nobody visits between October and March. The owner is away until spring and her rules are pinned beside the key board in her own handwriting: no guests. The season still has an instalment to make and the boiler eats oil. Then somebody knocks: after the last bus, in the rain, with cash and no booking, and a reason they would rather not give. You decide who gets a key, and which room.
